correctness.rationale: Centering with t=2x+1 gives 8G=t^4+6t²+1. For t≡±1 mod 3 the target is 1 mod 3 and the derivative is a unit, giving exactly one root per class at every finite level and full 3-adic coverage of that output ball. On t=3s the normalized displacement is H(s)^2, with H(s)=sR(s) and R(s) the Hensel square root of 1+(3/2)s² congruent to 1. Factoring R(s)^2−R(u)^2 shows H(s)−H(u) is s−u times a factor congruent to 1 modulo 3; hence H induces a bijection at each precision and on the inverse limit. The singular outputs are c+27H(s)^2/4, disjoint from the first ball. For k≤2 the singular branch contains 3^(k−1) inputs and one output. For k≥3 there are nine lifts from each square root modulo 3^(k−3) to s modulo 3^(k−1), including the modulus-one case k=3. At j>0 a zero square has 3^floor(j/2) roots; an even positive or zero valuation 2a<j with square unit part has 2·3^a, and other targets have none. Summing the image by attained valuations gives Q_3 and the limit 1/3+(3/8)/27=25/72. Independent finite replay compared each target for k=1…9, confirming counts 2,4,10,29,85,254,760,2279,6835 and all fiber sizes; the all-k argument is analytic, not inferred from this check.
